title: Old-Time Cabbage Storage
subtitle: Tips From a 1940s USDA Bulletin
desc: Old-time cabbage storage from a 1940s USDA Farmers' Bulletin: pull firm heads roots and all, keep them cold and moist near 32°F, and store them outdoors in a straw-lined trench, since cabbage odor spreads through a house cellar. Root cellar wisdom for winter.

title: How to Can Applesauce
subtitle: USDA Water Bath Method
items: Hot pack: reheat to a boil
desc: How to can homemade applesauce safely in a boiling water bath, following the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning: hot pack, 1/2-inch headspace, 15 minutes for pints and 20 for quarts at 0–1,000 ft, with longer times at higher altitudes.

title: How to Freeze Pumpkin Puree
subtitle: Easy Fall Food Preservation
desc: How to freeze pumpkin puree for pies, breads and soups: cook until soft, mash, cool quickly and pack with headspace. Freezing is the safe choice, because mashed pumpkin should never be home canned.

title: Stay Warm in a Power Outage
subtitle: Winter Storm Safety Tips
desc: How to stay warm when the power goes out in winter: heat one closed-off room, dress in layers and cover windows, and avoid carbon monoxide by never using grills, camp stoves or generators indoors. Essential winter storm and off grid prep.

title: Plant Garlic in the Fall
subtitle: Big Bulbs Next Summer
desc: How to plant garlic in the fall for a big summer harvest: separate cloves, plant them pointed end up 2 inches deep and 6 inches apart before the ground freezes, then mulch with straw. An easy beginner vegetable garden project.
